source: Daw, Gershman, Seymour, Dayan, Dolan (2011) Model-based influences on humans' choices and striatal prediction errors
finding: Humans on a two-step task used both model-free and model-based learning. Ventral striatal BOLD prediction errors were not purely model-free. They carried model-based information too, in the proportion that fit each person's choices.
numbers: N=17, 201 trials each. Reward main effect p<1e-8; reward x transition interaction p<5e-5 (rejects pure reinforcement). Hybrid model: median model-free weight 61% (model-based 39%), lambda median 0.57. Hybrid model exceedance probability 92%; 48% of population hybrid, 18% pure TD. Right ventral striatum: neural model-based loading correlated with behavioural weight w (p<.01 small-volume corrected).
quote: the signal reflected both model-free and model-based predictions in proportions matching those that best explained choice behavior
limits: Small N. vmPFC conjunction survived whole-brain correction only at a relaxed threshold (p<.005 uncorrected). fMRI BOLD cannot isolate dopamine spikes.
agent_relevance: The textbook dopamine/RPE signal is already contaminated by model-based knowledge in humans. An agent loop cannot treat reward-error learning as a clean model-free module.

source: Daw, Gershman, Seymour, Dayan, Dolan (2011) Model-based influences on humans' choices and striatal prediction errors
finding: The two-step task gives a diagnostic: a model-free learner repeats a rewarded first choice even after a rare transition; a model-based learner switches. Subjects showed a mix.
numbers: Reward effect positive in 14/17 individuals; interaction positive in 10/17 (7 had both). Mean 2 +/- 2 (SD) trials per subject missed the 2 s limit.
limits: Between-subject variability is large. Doll 2012 notes model-free learners with overlapping state codes can mimic model-based patterns.
agent_relevance: A cheap behavioural signature (stay/switch by reward x transition) separates habit-like from planning-like policies. It could label whether an LLM agent's policy reuses past reward or reasons over a model.

source: Doll, Simon, Daw (2012) The ubiquity of model-based reinforcement learning
finding: Review of evidence that model-based information shows up in striatal and dopaminergic prediction errors, with explicit caveats about what that evidence can show.
numbers: Cites Daw 2011 (ventral striatum), Simon and Daw 2011 (putamen values follow model-based updating), Glascher 2010, Bromberg-Martin 2010 (dopamine neurons carry information a model-free learner lacks). No new data.
limits: Model-free learners with generalising state representations can mimic model-based behaviour. Overtraining (habit) confounds putamen results. Animal electrophysiology for model-based signals was largely missing in 2012. Dopamine pharmacology results are mixed.
agent_relevance: Moderators of model-based control: favoured by high uncertainty; disfavoured after overtraining, low action-reward contiguity, high reward variability, and stress (time cost of planning). The same levers decide when an agent should plan versus reuse cached answers.

source: Sadacca, Jones, Schoenbaum (2016, eLife) Midbrain dopamine neurons compute inferred and cached value prediction errors in a common framework
finding: Rat VTA dopamine neurons responded to the inferred value of a cue never paired with reward (sensory preconditioning), in the same way as to cached value. Standard TD cannot do this.
numbers: 14 rats, 632 VTA neurons, 304 putative dopamine neurons in conditioning. Probe test: 102 neurons, 52 putative dopamine. B>D firing t(51)=4.40 p<.001; A>C (inferred) t(51)=5.02 p<.001; correlation of the two effects r(50)=0.63 p<.001. Cue-vs-reward shift over conditioning r(302)=0.24 p<.01.
limits: The classic cue shift was weak (r=0.24). Cells classified by response profile, not tagged optogenetically in this study. Tonic neurons showed no significant cached-inferred correlation (r(37)=0.26, p=0.11).
agent_relevance: Prediction-error signals can be driven by inference over a learned model, not only by cached reward history. Supports pairing an agent's reward-error step with a world model.

source: Sharpe et al. (2020, Nat Commun) Dopamine transients do not act as model-free prediction errors during associative learning
finding: Optogenetic activation of rat VTA dopamine cells during cue learning produced associative (model-based) learning but did not give the cue cached value, contradicting a pure model-free TD prediction.
numbers: Exp 1: ChR2 n=8, eYFP n=8. Conditioned reinforcement to preconditioned cue C: cue x group F(1,14)=0.004, p=0.952. Probe test: cue x group F(1,14)=5.060, p=0.041; C>D in ChR2 only, F(1,14)=6.578, p=0.022. Exp 3 gave 280 stimulated trials with no value gain.
quote: dopamine transients support associative, rather than model-free, learning
limits: Artificial stimulation, small groups, rats. Authors say TD errors might still exist endogenously.
agent_relevance: Even a causal dopamine pulse can teach 'what predicts what' rather than 'how good'. A single scalar reward error may serve structure learning, not only value updates.

source: Maes et al. (2020, Nat Neurosci) Causal evidence supporting the proposal that dopamine transients function as temporal difference prediction errors
finding: Opposing result: shunting cue-evoked dopamine with halorhodopsin blocked second-order conditioning but did not disrupt blocking. That is what a TD prediction error predicts and a pure value signal does not.
numbers: n=16 rats. Second-order test: responding to C lower than D, z=1.9, p=0.03, r=0.34. Blocking intact: blocked X vs Y z=0.05, p=0.48, r=0.009; blocking effect z=2.22, p=0.01, r=0.39.
limits: Effects modest (r=0.34 to 0.39), p values near .03. Rats, one lab. Partly conflicts with Sharpe 2020 but tests necessity, not sufficiency.
agent_relevance: Evidence is split on whether dopamine pulses are TD errors. Treat the RPE-as-learning-signal claim as supported in some designs and challenged in others.

source: Jeong et al. (2022, Science) Mesolimbic dopamine release conveys causal associations
finding: Mouse nucleus accumbens dopamine failed several key TD-RPE predictions and matched a retrospective causal-association model (ANCCR) instead.
numbers: n=7 to 8 mice per test, dLight 1.3b photometry. Test 1: response to unpredicted reward rises with experience, t(7)=4.40 p=0.0031. Test 2: positive correlation with prior interval t(7)=5.95 p=5.7e-4. Test 4: cue-reward delay 3 s to 9 s, no cue-response change. Test 6: cue response stays positive after extinction t(6)=5.67 p=0.0013. Tests 9 to 11: no backpropagation; inhibited animals still learned.
limits: Small N. Some tests not significant (change-trial p=0.0531). Authors note TD can be rescued with unlimited state-space assumptions. Only NAc core measured.
agent_relevance: Rival account: dopamine marks causal relevance to meaningful events, not value error. Suggests agent credit assignment should look backward from outcomes to likely causes.

source: Dabney et al. (2020, Nature) A distributional code for value in dopamine-based reinforcement learning
finding: Mouse VTA dopamine neurons show diverse optimism and pessimism, as distributional RL predicts, not one shared error.
numbers: 40 optogenetically identified neurons (magnitude task), 31 in probability task from 5 mice. Reversal-point split-half R=0.58 p=1.8e-5. 10/31 optimistic and 9/31 pessimistic cells (chance about 3/31). ANOVA F(30,3335)=4.31 p=6e-14. Mean asymmetry tau=0.48. Asymmetry vs reversal point p=8.1e-5.
limits: Few cells per animal; most recorded in different sessions. Noise-added TD or asymmetric learning-rate models can mimic diversity under some analyses. Decoding reported qualitatively. Stable cell ranking untested.
agent_relevance: Distributional value is a concrete design hint: keep a spread of optimistic and pessimistic estimates instead of a single mean score.

source: Taira et al. (2024, J Neurosci) Dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens core encodes the general excitatory components of learning
finding: Nucleus accumbens core dopamine behaved like general excitation of learning, not sensory-specific prediction error. Backward conditioning shifted release in a way standard TD cannot explain.
numbers: 9 rats; forward n=7, omission and reversal n=5, 8 sessions, GRAB-DA2m photometry at 20 Hz. No congruent vs incongruent compound difference despite a behavioural difference. Unexpected cue omission gave larger cue release than expected cues.
limits: Correlational photometry. Males only. n=5 in omission tests. Compound cues were novel and salient, a confound.
agent_relevance: Another documented anomaly: dopamine can carry non-value, general-purpose learning signals. Weakens any claim that a scalar RPE is the full learning signal.

source: Test-retest reliability of reinforcement learning parameters (Behav Res Methods 2024)
finding: Reliability problem: individual learning-rate parameters from RL tasks are unstable over five weeks.
numbers: Bandit N=69, reversal N=47, 5 weeks apart. Parameter ICC .02 to .52 (bandit), .01 to .71 (reversal). Personality ICC .67 to .93; Raven r=.60. Win-stay ICC .53 (bandit), .62 (reversal). Accuracy ICC .23 (bandit).
limits: Online samples. Simulations showed reliability could be detected, so the instability is real. Earlier studies: learning-rate reliability .16 to .59 (Waltmann 2022).
agent_relevance: Fitted learning rates are weak individual-difference measures. Do not tune an agent's learning-rate-like setting on one run and expect it to transfer.

source: Demircan, Saanum, Jagadish, Binz, Schulz (2024) Sparse autoencoders reveal temporal difference learning in large language models
finding: Llama 3 70B learns two-step RL tasks in context. Sparse autoencoder latents in its residual stream track TD errors and Q-values, and lesioning them hurts behaviour.
numbers: Block 34 SAE latent r=0.58 with Q-learning TD error. SAEs trained on 18000 residual representations, 30 epochs. Deactivating the TD latent gave worse task performance; deactivating the lowest-correlation latent did not. Larger task: TD latents r>=0.75 in blocks 40 onward; lesioning degraded action prediction. Repetition model NLL 5745 (worse than chance).
quote: representations emerge despite the model only being trained to predict the next token
limits: Preprint (ICLR 2025). Correlational by SAE; one model. Behaviour is predicting a Q-learner's actions, not acting.
agent_relevance: First direct evidence that next-token training can yield TD-error-like internal features. Suggests in-context rewards can act as a learning signal without weight updates.

source: Demircan, Saanum, Jagadish, Binz, Schulz (2024) Sparse autoencoders reveal temporal difference learning in large language models
finding: In graph learning with no reward, Llama's latents fit successor-representation TD signals better than a model-based surprise signal.
numbers: Max r with SR 0.62 vs transition matrix 0.49; TD error r=0.60 vs surprise r=0.18. Lesion of the best TD latent (block 64) cut next-state accuracy from 24.3% to 18.9% (ceiling 25%).
limits: Single model. Absolute accuracy is low, ceiling 25%. TD correlations recovered quickly after lesion.
agent_relevance: Model-free-like (SR) learning and model-based knowledge coexist inside the LLM, echoing Daw 2011 in humans.

source: Demircan, Saanum, Jagadish, Binz, Schulz (2024) Sparse autoencoders reveal temporal difference learning in large language models
finding: Control: Llama predicts a Q-learner's actions better with true rewards than with randomised +1/-1 rewards, so it uses reward and not only action patterns.
numbers: Reward-intact prompt beat random-reward prompt on action prediction (Fig 4A). Exact gap not extracted.
limits: No scalar effect size read from the text.
agent_relevance: In-context reward changes the model's internal state, so feedback integration in an agent loop is a real mechanism.

source: Demircan, Saanum, Jagadish, Binz, Schulz (2024) Sparse autoencoders reveal temporal difference learning in large language models
finding: Caution on the LLM-RPE claim: the best latent correlation is moderate and correlation is not proof of the same algorithm.
numbers: r=0.58 (best latent, two-step); r>=0.75 in selected blocks of the larger task. Myopic reward error also correlated highly.
limits: TD and reward-only explanations are partly confounded.
agent_relevance: Claim only that error-tracking features exist and matter causally, not that LLMs implement dopamine-like RPE.

source: Monea, Bosselut, Brantley, Artzi (2025, COLM) LLMs are in-context bandit reinforcement learners
finding: LLMs learn from scalar reward in context (bandit ICRL) with no gold labels, but only if exploration is encouraged and negative feedback is handled carefully.
numbers: Qwen2.5-7B on Banking77 (77 labels): 6.2% zero-shot to 72.2% with Stochastic ICRL. Llama gains 28.6 to 74.4 points, Qwen 29.2 to 68.4 points over zero-shot. Tested 0.5B to 72B. Stochastic ICRL robust to 10% inverted rewards.
quote: underscoring fundamental limitations in their implicit reasoning about errors
limits: Naive ICRL unstable, with sudden dips. Positive-reward-only context works best; learning from negative rewards is weak. Classification bandits only.
agent_relevance: Models learn from positive examples they found themselves, not from error signals. A scaffold should turn failures into explicit reasoning text.

source: Monea, Bosselut, Brantley, Artzi (2025, COLM) LLMs are in-context bandit reinforcement learners
finding: ICRL benefit scales with model size, and the ranking of methods is stable across sizes.
numbers: Qwen2.5 0.5B to 72B. Stochastic prompt sampling with p_keep=0.1 at temperature 1.0 vs Naive+ at temperature 2.0.
limits: Per-size numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Reward-driven in-context learning pays most at larger scale; small agent loops may not benefit.

source: Reward Is Enough: LLMs are in-context reinforcement learners (arXiv 2506.06303)
finding: Prompting a model with its own past answers and scalar rewards (ICRL) beat Reflexion, Self-Refine and Best-of-N on three benchmarks.
numbers: Game of 24 (100 problems, 50 trials): ICRL Preset 90%, Autonomous 84% vs Best-of-N 49%, Long-CoT 47%, Self-Refine 47%, Reflexion 44%, CoT 6%. ScienceWorld (max 100): ICRL 88 vs Self-Refine 83, Best-of-N 75. Creative writing LC win rate vs Best-of-N 93.81 +/- 1.01%.
limits: One model per benchmark (GPT-4.1 or 4.1 mini). Self-reward in some tasks; creative-writing reward is coherence against one reference. Gains fell with no rewards or a 3-episode context. Preprint; read via page summary.
agent_relevance: Scalar reward fed back into context is a cheap loop component. Gains depend on long history and an explore/exploit instruction.

source: Gershman et al. (2024, Nat Neurosci) Explaining dopamine through prediction errors and beyond
finding: Not opened: Gershman, Assad, Datta, Linderman, Sabatini, Uchida, Wilbrecht (2024) say the original RPE account is too simple on ramps, sensory/motor responses and action selection, yet a generalised prediction error covers them.
numbers: Seen only in search snippets.
limits: Not opened; the publisher page redirected to a login.
agent_relevance: Both sides agree the simple scalar-RPE story needs extension.

source: Gershman and Uchida (2019) Believing in dopamine
finding: Not opened: Gershman and Uchida (2019) argue dopamine reflects a belief-state prediction error, which handles several anomalies.
numbers: No numbers read; fetch blocked by captcha.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: An explicit belief state about hidden causes, not only observed cues, drives the error. Supports giving an agent an explicit belief state.

source: Schultz, Dayan, Montague (1997) A neural substrate of prediction and reward
finding: Not opened: Schultz, Dayan, Montague (1997). Monkey dopamine neurons fire to unexpected reward, shift to the cue after learning, and dip when an expected reward is omitted, matching a TD error.
numbers: No numbers read this session.
limits: Not opened. Original recordings came from few monkeys, identified by waveform, a later point of dispute.
agent_relevance: The reference model that every later row tests.

source: The Transmitter (2024) Does a new theory of dopamine replace the classic model?
finding: Not opened: The Transmitter commentary reports that Jeong 2022 challenged TD, and that simple models fail on dopamine while tuned or modified models can fit.
numbers: Search snippet only.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Field status in 2024 is contested, not settled.

source: Jacob et al. (2024, Nat Neurosci) dopamine RPE and perceived locus of control
finding: Not opened: search snippet says Jacob et al. 2024 (Nat Neurosci) found dopaminergic reward prediction errors reflect an agent's perceived locus of control.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Not opened; citation unverified beyond the snippet.
agent_relevance: Perceived control as a moderator: an agent that can influence outcomes may weight errors differently.

source: Alexander and Gershman (2021) Representation learning with reward prediction errors
finding: Not opened: Alexander and Gershman (2021 preprint) propose dopamine prediction errors also support learning adaptive state representations.
numbers: Search snippet only.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Error signals may shape representations, not just values; relevant to agents that rewrite their own problem framing.

source: Sharpe et al. (2020, Nat Commun) Dopamine transients do not act as model-free prediction errors during associative learning
finding: Experiment 2 used 28 Long-Evans TH-Cre rats. Authors argue earlier optogenetic studies did not test value separately from association, so their 'value' reading was untested.
numbers: Exp 1 n=8 vs 8. Exp 2 n=28. Exp 3 delivered 280 stimulated trials with no extra conditioned reinforcement for the paired cue.
limits: Rival reading: endogenous TD errors may differ from imposed 1 s stimulation. Rats only.
agent_relevance: Separate the two measures when testing any agent: whether it learned a relation versus whether it assigned value.

source: Dabney et al. (2020, Nature) A distributional code for value in dopamine-based reinforcement learning
finding: Decoding from recorded cell diversity recovered the reward distribution; classical TD simulation did not. Diversity alone was not enough, the specific pattern mattered.
numbers: GABA control cells (one animal): 12/36 optimistic, 11/36 pessimistic in the probability task. Within top animal, dopamine 4/17 optimistic, 5/17 pessimistic; F(15,1652)=4.02 p=3e-7.
limits: No numerical decoding fit metric was in the text read.
agent_relevance: Ensembles of agents with different risk attitudes can represent uncertainty better than one averaged agent.

source: Taira et al. (2024, J Neurosci) Dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens core encodes the general excitatory components of learning
finding: Backward conditioning: reward-evoked release grew and cue-evoked release shrank over sessions, though reward value stayed constant. Standard TD would not predict this.
numbers: Backward conditioning 8 sessions, 12 presentations per association per session; recorded on sessions 1, 4, 8.
limits: Photometry gives bulk signal. No causal silencing. Males only.
agent_relevance: A prediction-error-like change in signal need not mean value learning; check controls before crediting a reward-error mechanism.
